title: Train a Tiny GPT End to End
summary: Put the transformer block to work: a byte-level tokenizer, shifted batches, a 3.35-million-parameter GPT, cross-entropy, an AdamW loop with gradient clipping, a sampler and a validation check. By the end you can train a model on a laptop and read what it writes.
objectives: Build a byte-level tokenizer and explain why UTF-8 makes Hindi cost about 2.6 tokens per character
Produce (x, y) batches by shifting a random window one position and compute tokens per step as B·n
Assemble embeddings, transformer blocks, a final norm and an LM head into a GPT and count its parameters by hand
Write a training loop with AdamW and gradient clipping, and check that the first loss is close to ln V
Generate text with temperature, top-k and top-p, and use validation loss and perplexity to spot overfitting
prerequisites: This lesson assumes the transformer block you built in [Attention in code](/learn/model-foundations/attention-in-code). The theory it turns into code comes from [How a network learns](/learn/model-foundations/how-networks-learn) (loss, gradient descent, overfitting), [Tokenization](/learn/model-foundations/tokenization) (bytes and UTF-8) and [Sampling](/learn/model-foundations/sampling) (temperature, top-k, top-p, perplexity). You need Python and PyTorch installed; a CPU is enough for the small config.
